description:
Returns a bundle-ready quote for the requested assets or units, plus expected best/worst average prices and maximum executable liquidity.

The endpoint optimizes for successful target-aware bundle execution under contention: `takeable_offers` are best-priced per-offer caps and their total can exceed the requested target, giving a bundle executor fallback liquidity when earlier offers are partially consumed or skipped.

At most `limit` (default and maximum 10,000) best-priced takeable offers are walked and returned; prices and availability always describe exactly the returned window. A request that cannot fill within `limit` offers returns 422.

Use the returned takeable offers with a bundle abstraction that stops at your requested target and applies your max/min asset or unit protections. If you execute takeable offers independently with Midnight.take, do not submit every returned unit blindly: clamp each offer to your remaining target and current takeability, or you may execute more than intended.

If the requested size cannot be fully satisfied at quote time under the selected guard, the endpoint returns 422.

assets.description: Target assets amount. Provide exactly one of `assets` or `units`.

average_worst_price.description: Optional conservative average worst-price guard for the requested target. For `asks`, the returned `average_worst_price` is at or below this value; for `bids`, it is at or above it. The target-closing offer is clipped exactly when needed, and only whole additional fallback caps whose conservative bound remains inside the guard are returned. If the target itself cannot satisfy the guard, the request fails with 422. Mutually exclusive with `slippage`.

limit.description: Maximum number of best-priced takeable offers the quote may walk and return. Returned prices and availability describe exactly this window, and a request that cannot fill within `limit` offers returns 422. Maximum: 10000. Default: 10000.

market-id.description: Market ID whose book to quote (`market_id` in responses).

slippage.description: Optional slippage percentage used to derive a worst-price guard from the realized `average_best_price` for the requested target. The returned fallback window is trimmed until its conservative `average_worst_price` stays inside that guard. For `asks`, the guard increases by slippage; for `bids`, it decreases by slippage. The response reports the conservative bound, not the derived guard. Range: 0.1 to 100, with at most one decimal place. Mutually exclusive with `average_worst_price`.

units.description: Target unit amount. Provide exactly one of `assets` or `units`.

name: morpho_midnight_get_book_quote

market_id.description: Market id (32-byte hex) the offer belongs to.

ratifier_data.description: Mandatory data generated by the maker to verify the offer onchain.

units.description: Executable or currently reserved offer size in units.

valid_until.description: Inclusive Unix-second bound until which `offer` and `ratifier_data` stay executable as published; never exceeds `offer.expiry`. Refetch after it passes.

warning.description: Deprecated: still returned for now, but will become null in a future release and then be removed. Do not rely on it; `units` already is the amount you can take. Quote responses preserve this pre-quote book measurement after clipping. Makers can still see why their offers are limited on `GET /v0/midnight/takeable-offers`.

liquidation_cursor.description: Liquidation cursor for this collateral, scaled by 1e18. The protocol derives the maximum liquidation incentive factor from it.

lltv.description: Liquidation loan-to-value for this collateral, scaled by 1e18.

oracle.description: Oracle address used to price this collateral.

chain_id.description: EVM chain id the market lives on.

midnight.description: Address of the Midnight contract that owns the market.

callback.description: Settlement callback address. Use the zero address for empty callbacks. A Blue-backed buy uses a BlueBuyCallback registered to the maker by the chain's factory at or before the offer's creation block; a maker-chosen salt allows multiple callbacks.

callback_data.description: Settlement callback data. Use `0x` for empty callbacks. A Blue-backed buy uses the exact 160-byte ABI encoding of Morpho Blue `MarketParams` (`loanToken`, `collateralToken`, `oracle`, `irm`, `lltv`); `loanToken` must match the offer market.

continuous_fee_cap.description: Maximum market continuous fee the maker accepts; the offer is not takeable while the market continuous fee exceeds it. Decimal uint256 string.

data.description: Quote result and signed takeable-offer instructions.

available_assets.description: Maximum assets available from the returned takeable-offer caps if they remain executable. This can exceed the requested target so bundle execution has fallback liquidity.

available_units.description: Maximum units available from the returned takeable-offer caps if they remain executable. This can exceed the requested target so bundle execution has fallback liquidity.

average_best_price.description: Realized average price for the requested size filled against the returned offers in book order, applying the same per-offer rounding as onchain execution and rounded against the taker, so unit or asset guards derived from it stay executable.

average_worst_price.description: Conservative adverse-placement bound for the requested size across the returned offer caps. It fractionally relaxes full-offer selection at each cap's realized assets-per-unit rate and rounds the boundary against the taker, bounding every combination of full returned caps plus one target-closing partial. It is never more favorable than average_best_price and never echoes the caller's guard or a best-plus-slippage projection. Multiple offers that are all partially consumed after quoting can still require a fresh quote or execution-time minimum/maximum checks.

takeable_offers.description: Best-priced signed takeable-offer caps intended for target-aware bundle execution. Each `units` value is the maximum that offer may contribute, not an exact allocation for the requested target; the sum can exceed the requested size so a bundle executor can skip stale offers and still fill the target. If you call Midnight.take directly instead of using target-aware bundle execution, clamp each offer to your remaining target and current takeability, otherwise you may execute more than intended.

anyOf.description: Maker-controlled funds cannot back more units.
The maker's loan-token approval cannot back more units.
The underlying protocol cannot currently release more liquidity.
More units would increase rather than reduce the maker's position.
The maker's credit or debt position has no room for more units.
Asset and unit rounding prevents another meaningful unit from executing.
The callback was not registered to the maker at or before the offer's creation block.
The maker does not currently authorize the offer's ratifier.
Router simulation failed for the offer's group and market.
The offer is reserved for a specific taker and cannot be taken publicly.
The offer exceeds the maximum units allowed in one take.

limit_units.description: Maximum units allowed in one take.

anyOf.description: The offer's Ecrecover Merkle root was permanently canceled.
The maker has not currently ratified the offer's Setter Merkle root.

root.description: Setter Merkle root the maker has not currently ratified.

anyOf.description: The maker does not currently authorize the offer tree's signer.

signer.description: Tree signer the maker has not authorized.

anyOf.description: The offer was removed after its supported size fell below policy minimum.

observed_assets.description: Assets measured when the offer was removed.

TakeabilityWarningResponse.description: Primary warning discriminated by its machine-readable code.

data.description: Quote result and signed takeable-offer instructions.
